newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cenbank sees room for lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Czech cenbank sees room for lower rates.

text.p: Czech National Bank board member Jiri Pospisil said on Tuesday that an unexpectedly low June inflation result gave the central bank room to carefully lower interest rates.
In a brief interview with Reuters, Pospisil also said that the central bank expected end-year inflation to accelerate to just over 10 percent year-on-year, after several price deregulations bite.
"The (inflation) figures for June were better than we expected and make possible a further lowering of interest rates," Pospisil said.
He said that the central bank would continue its cautious approach to lowering rates, reacting to the situation on the market.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) on Tuesday released data showing overall prices jumped 1.2 percent month-on-month in June, forcing the year-on-year rate to 6.8 percent, up from June's record low of 6.3 percent.
The sliding average inflation figure, which uses 1993 as a base, edged down to 7.9 percent from 8.0 percent in May, and was down from 8.6 percent in May 1996.
The central bank hiked interest rates in May to combat a speculative attack on the crown, but was forced to float the currency on May 27.

Since then the CNB has taken a "soft landing" approach, lowering interest rates but keeping a close eye on possible speculative short-term positions in the crown which might signal another attack on the currency.

The central bank's repo rate, which has been gradually lowered in recent weeks from when it was 75 percent at the height of the crown attacks, was lowered to 16.50 percent on Tuesday from levels above 18 percent last week.

Pospisil, who is the executive director of the CNB's monetary division, said the central bank expected July's monthly inflation to top two percent as a series of state-controlled rents and energy prices are deregulated.
"December (year-on-year inflation) growth will be slightly higher than 10 percent," he said, adding that the sliding average was seen at "slightly under" 10 percent.
Year-end 1996 inflation was 8.6 percent, year-on-year, while the sliding average for the year was 8.8 percent.
